subject: Mathematics
overall_notes: Round 2 lifts land cleanly. Alignment 4: C4 step 2 (data) is the explicit target; lesson cross-references Day 1 ('Yesterday Lesson 1 asked the math questions') and forward-bridges to Day 3 ('Tomorrow Lesson 3 — C4.2 uses today's DATA to PREDICT'). Pedagogical_depth 4: count-vs-estimate trap is named with CGI (Carpenter, Fennema & Franke) and Lehrer & Schauble (2002) citations; recovery_moves branches into 3 diagnostics (A: can count but estimates; B: can't count, drop to 10-cluster singles; C: counts but doesn't record, pre-printed tally rows). Instructional_balance 4: Mira/Tom puppets explicitly OPTIONAL with substitutes; everyday materials (chart paper, counters, number line); 12/25/13 = 50 min realistic for G2; explicit NO-MATERIALS PATH (claps/fingers, body becomes data table). Clarity_voice 4: Mira anchors minds_on + consolidation; quotable refrain 'COUNT IT, don't GUESS IT — every tally tells the truth!' chanted 3x at exit; child-friendly vocab; 'I can' success criteria. Mathematical_authenticity 4: STRATEGY COMPARE step (singles vs groups-of-five vs two-colour counters) lets children compare strategies and cites Lehrer & Schauble on speed-of-creation vs speed-of-reuse; tally-and-total framed as prerequisite for prediction. Lesson_worksheet_consistency 4: Part 1 visual cluster tally probe (14 book icons, 9 bus icons) requires PRODUCING the count rather than copying — transfer task; Part 3 generalises to child's own town life (transfer with justification).
